symptom: With `run --local --watch` serving an app, a change made by `mxcli exec` was applied 4.2-5.2 s after exec had exited, although the log line said "applied via reload in 2.0s". Measured on a blank Mendix 11.16.0 app over eleven changes.
cause: The watch loop cannot see a write end. It polled the source mtime once a second and then waited for two more unchanged polls (settleSource) before building, so that a multi-file exec is never built half-written. For a writer that has already exited that is about 2.7 s of waiting for nothing.
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/watchwriter.go (BeginModelWrite, watchWriterGate), cmd/mxcli/docker/runlocal.go (watchAndApply wakes every 100 ms for the signal and skips the settle after one), cmd/mxcli/cmd_exec.go and cmd/mxcli/oneliner.go (the callers)
insight: The duration a loop prints for its own work is not the latency its user feels: subtract the two and the difference is where to look. The settle was the right answer to a writer that cannot say it is done and the wrong one for mxcli's own commands, which can. A pid-named marker plus a stamp covers the three cases without a protocol: marker present and pid alive is 'writing, do not build', stamp changed is 'done, build now', marker present and pid dead is 'done, however it ended'. Register the signal's defer before the executor's Close so it runs after the last write. Control, same app and session: an unsignalled write (touching the .mpr) still took 4.2 s, a signalled exec 2.2-2.5 s; an exec that changed nothing started no build.
